rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good counsel includes telling the self to acknowledge God’s provision and repay blessings through obedience.
rows.anchor: المعروف مع النفس أن يقول : أكلت رزق الله ونعمه فأدي شكر نعمته بامتثال أوامره ونواهيه

rows.speaker: عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet urges believers to dissolve food through prayer and remembrance.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام"أذيبوا طعامكم بالصلاة والذكر"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After meals, the minimum is two rakʿas, one hundred glorifications, or a Qur’an portion; remembrance prevents hardness and fulfills gratitude.
rows.anchor: وأقل ذلك أن يصلي ركعتين أو يسبح مائة تسبيحة أو يقرأ جزءا من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the wealth of knowledge and treasures of gnosis should not be handed to or discussed before unready common people.
rows.anchor: إشارة أخرى وهي أن أموال العلوم وكنوز المعارف لا تؤتى لغير أهلها من العوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story and Persian verse warn that sacred knowledge is wasted when broadcast among unfit hearers.
rows.anchor:
لا يباع الإبل في سوق الدجاج.
درغست باسفله كفت ازعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians should test minors before puberty by observing religious soundness and their ability to manage money well.
rows.anchor: واختبروا أيها الأولياء والأوصياء من ليس من اليتامى بين السفه قبل البلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For prospective traders, test competence by entrusting them with money for buying and selling.
rows.anchor: فإن كانوا من أهل التجارة فبأن تعطوهم من المال ما يتصرفون فيه بيعا وابتياعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those managing estates and households, entrust suitable expenses to them to reveal their judgment.
rows.anchor: وإن كانوا ممن له ضياع وأهل وخدم فبأن تعطوا منه ما يصرفونه إلى نفقة عبيدهم وخدمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching marriage age means puberty, when a person becomes eligible for marriage.
rows.anchor: {حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح} بأن يحتلموا لأنهم يصلحون عنده للنكاح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ānastum means that guardians have observed and ascertained maturity of judgment.
rows.anchor: {فإن ءانستم} أي : شاهدتم وتبينتم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd requires religious soundness and the ability to manage assets without incapacity or waste.
rows.anchor: {منهم رشدا} صلاحا في دينهم واهتداء إلى وجوه التصرفات من غير عجز وتبذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once puberty and sound judgment are established, transfer the orphan’s property without delay.
rows.anchor: {فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم} من غير تأخير عن حد البلوغ.

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad infer that an adult who remains wasteful or incapable never receives the property.
rows.anchor: وبه أخذ أبو يوسف ومحمد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa delays transfer until age twenty-five, seven years beyond the assumed age of puberty, then releases it even without observed prudence.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة ينتظر إلى خمس وعشرين سنة لأن البلوغ بالسن ثماني عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase forbids consuming the estate wrongfully and wastefully; it does not permit small unlawful consumption.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه إباحة القليل وتحريم الإسراف بل هو بيان أنه إسراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians who hurry to spend fear that the orphans will mature, reclaim the estate, and restrict their spending.
rows.anchor: {وبدارا} أي مبادرين ومسارعين إلى إنفاقها مخافة {أن يكبروا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian must abstain from the estate, content with personal provision to protect the orphan and its assets.
rows.anchor: {ومن كان غنيا} من الأولياء والأوصياء فليتنزه عن أكلها وليمتنع وليقنع بما آتاه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiafaf is more emphatic than abstinence: the wealthy guardian should actively seek greater chastity.
rows.anchor: واستعفف أبلغ من عف كأنه يطلب زيادة العفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poor guardian may take a customary lawful amount for necessary needs and fair compensation for work, showing a trustee’s service-based right.
rows.anchor: {فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} أي بما عرف في الشرع بقدر حاجته الضرورية وأجرة سعيه وخدمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses should attest that the heirs received the estate, protecting the guardian from suspicion and dispute and clearing responsibility.
rows.anchor: {فأشهدوا عليهم} بأنهم تسلموها وقبضوها وبرئت منها ذممكم

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s Hanafi school does not make witnesses obligatory and accepts the guardian’s sworn statement of delivery.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يكن واجبا عند أصحابنا فإن الوصي مصدق في الدفع مع اليمين

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi require proof and do not accept a guardian’s claim of delivery without witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك والشافعي لا يصدق في دعواه إلا بالبينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God records and preserves deeds; especially avoid the grave sin of taking an orphan’s rights and seek forgiveness before the afterlife.
rows.anchor: {وكفى بالله} الباء صلة {حسيبا} محاسبا وحافظا لأعمال خلقه فلا تخالفوا ما أمرتم به

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that a wronged person must be appeased before the Hereafter, when good deeds are transferred or the victim’s sins are imposed.
rows.anchor: من كانت عنده مظلمة لأخيه أو شيء فليتحلله منه اليوم من قبل أن لا يكون دينار ولا درهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who has repented from many wrongs but cannot find the victims should increase good deeds and keep some acts sincerely private, hoping for divine reconciliation.
rows.anchor: فليكثر من حسناته ليوم القصاص وليسر ببعض الحسنات بينه وبين الله بكمال الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After affirming the reality of resurrection and judgment, deniers are told to taste the punishment they rejected in worldly life.
rows.anchor: قالوا بلى وربنا} إنه لحق {قال فذوقوا العذاب} الذي عاينتموه {بما كنتم تكفرون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taste” signals that each punishment they experience is followed by something worse.
rows.anchor: وخص لفظ الذوق للإشارة إلى أن ما يجدونه من العذاب في كل حال هو ما يجده الذائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative of regret is figurative hyperbole: they call regret to arrive now, like calling woe, highlighting their foolish past choices.
rows.anchor: ونداؤها مجاز لأن الحسرة لا يتأتى منها الإقبال وإنما المعنى على المبالغة في شدة التحسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regret neglecting the Hour, failing to believe in it and prepare through good deeds; tafrīṭ means leaving what one could have done.
rows.anchor: على تفريطنا في شأن الساعة وتقصيرنا في مراعاة حقها والاستعداد لها بالإيمان بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about carrying burdens describes their state as they speak; awzār are sins named as heavy loads.
rows.anchor: {وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم} حال من فاعل قالوا ، والأوزار جمع وزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling sins loads and placing them on backs is metaphor, since burdens belong to bodies; backs are mentioned because people ordinarily carry weight there.
rows.anchor: والحمل من توابع الأعيان الكثيفة لا من عوارض المعاني فلا يوصف به العرض إلا على سبيل التمثيل والتشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast is that they mourn the good deeds they failed to do while physically bearing the sins they did commit.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم يتحسرون على ما لم يعملوا من الحسنات والحال إنهم يحملون أوزار ما عملوا من السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase means how evil a load they bear.
rows.anchor: {ألا سآء ما يزرون} أي : بئس شيئا يزرون ، أي : يحملون وزرهم.

rows.speaker: السدي وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others report that a believer meets a beautiful, fragrant form of his good deeds after rising and rides it, as in the gathering of the God-conscious as mounted guests.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وغيره : إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أحسن شيء صورة وأطيبه ريحا

rows.speaker: السدي وغيره
rows.claim: The unbeliever instead meets an ugly, foul-smelling embodiment of evil deeds that says it rode him in life and now rides him.
rows.anchor: وأما الكافر : فيستقبله أقبح شيء صورة وأنتنه ريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this report, carrying deeds is literal because deeds take visible forms in the afterlife although they are accidents here.
rows.anchor: فيكون الحمل على حقيقته لأن للأعمال صورا تظهر في الآخرة وإن كان نفسها إعراضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Existence itself is the greatest burden because it gives rise to other sins and blocks the seeker; repent of all and efface the self in the path of truth.
rows.anchor: ذنب الوجود فوق الكل ؛ إذ هو الباعث على سائر الأوزار وهو ثقل مانع عن السلوك

rows.speaker: حافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s verse rejects self-centered thought and opinion in the world of spiritual freedom, treating self-regard as unbelief in that path.
rows.anchor:
فكر خود ورأى خود در عالم رندى نيست
كفرست درين مذهب خود بيني وخودر رأيي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say one cannot escape the self by means of the self; only God enables release.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن الخروج من النفس بالنفس وإنما يمكن الخروج من النفس بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi teaches that remembrance moistens and softens the heart; without it, ego and desire harden it and the limbs resist obedience like a dead tree fit for cutting.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى يرطب القلب ويلينه فإذا خلا عن الذكر أصابته حرارة النفس ونار الشهوات فقسا ويبس

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: Remembrance, divine unity, and following their people are the foundations of spiritual life.
rows.anchor: فالذكر والتوحيد والاتباع إلى أهله هو أصل الأصول

rows.speaker: علي بن الموفق
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Muwaffaq dreamed that heavenly maidens washed his feet after he gave up his litter and joined other pilgrims on foot; they counted him among them because he loved their company.
rows.anchor: حججت سنة من السنين في محمل فرأيت رجالا ، فأحببت المشي معهم فنزلت وأركبت واحدا في المحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story teaches that sound-hearted companionship with a saint benefits; following and hearing the Prophet could remove deniers’ burdens and lead them to Paradise, though God guides whom He wills.
rows.anchor: هذه حال من مشى مع ولي باعتقاد صحيح فكيف مع نبي فلو أن كفار مكة ومشركي العرب استمعوا إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people argued about his faith and threatened that their idols would harm him if he abandoned them.
rows.anchor: {وحآجه قومه} أي : جادلوه في دينه وهددوه بالأصنام أن تصيبه بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic form is an assimilation of two nūns in the original أتحاجونني, meaning “are you disputing with me?”
rows.anchor: أتحاجوانى} بنون ثقيلة أصله أتحاجونني بنونين أولاهما نون الرفع والثانية نون الوقاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s argument concerns God’s oneness, and he says God has guided him to truth.
rows.anchor: {فى الله} أي في شأنه تعالى ووحدانيته {وقد هداان} أي : والحال إن الله تعالى هداني إلى الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not fear the idols because they have no power to cause harm.
rows.anchor: {ولا أخاف ما تشركون به} أي : ما تشركون به تعالى من الأصنام أن يصيبني بسوء لعدم قدرتها على شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is connected, with an omitted time: he fears no idol at any time unless God wills an injury through them; the idols themselves have no causal power.
rows.anchor: استثناء متصل والمستثنى منه وقت محذوف والتقدير لا أخاف معبوداتكم في وقت من الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge explains the exception: He may decree harm to reach Abraham through them for some other reason, not through their power.
rows.anchor:
{وسع ربى كل شىء علما} كأنه تعليل
57
للاستثناء أي أحاط بكل شيء علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham calls them to reflect that lifeless idols cannot benefit or harm him.
rows.anchor: {أفلا تتذكرون} أي : أتعرضون عن التأمل في أن آلهتكم جمادات غير قادرة على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “how could I fear” is a denial that idols, which neither harm nor benefit, are truly fearsome.
rows.anchor: {وكيف أخاف مآ أشركتم} بالله من الأصنام وهي لا تضر ولا تنفع والاستفهام إنكار الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast is that Abraham fears powerless objects while his opponents ignore the greatest danger, associating created things with the incomparable God.
rows.anchor: {ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله} حال من ضمير أخاف بتقدير مبتدأ أي وكيف أخاف أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Authority” means proof; the sarcastic phrasing signals that religious claims must rest on evidence revealed by God.
rows.anchor: {عليكم سلطانا} أي : حجة وبرهانا على طريقة التهكم مع الإيذان بأن الأمور الدينية لا يعول فيها إلا على الحجة المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks whether his monotheist party or the idolaters are more entitled to security.
rows.anchor: {فأى الفريقين أحق بالامن} أنحن أم أنتم.

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Suʿud explains the two parties as the group secure where safety belongs and the group secure where fear belongs.
rows.anchor: قال المولى أبو السعود : المراد بالفريقين الفريق الآمن في محل الأمن والفريق الآمن في محل الخوف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure believers are those who do not mix faith with shirk; idolaters wrongly claim idol worship completes their faith as a means of approach and intercession.
rows.anchor: لم يخلطوه {بظلم} أي : بشرك كما يفعله الفريق المشركون حيث يزعمون أنهم يؤمنون بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols’ claimed role is refuted by the idolaters’ own claim that they worship them only to bring them nearer to God.
rows.anchor: ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونآ إلى الله زلفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the believers free of shirk have security from punishment.
rows.anchor: {أولئك لهم الامن} فقط من العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those believers are guided to truth, while everyone outside their group is in manifest error.
rows.anchor: {وهم مهتدون} إلى الحق ومن عداهم في ضلال مبين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to Abraham’s proof from the signs in 6:76–82; a hujja is composed speech that supports inference.
rows.anchor: {وتلك} إشارة إلى ما احتج به إبراهيم على قومه من قوله : {فلما جن} (الأنعام : 76) إلى قوله : {وهم مهتدون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward path advances from recognizing God’s acts, to witnessing His attributes, then to realization of His existence and essence in unveiling, whose arrival has no final limit.
rows.anchor:
محجة السلوك إلى الله تعالى.
إنما هي تحقق بالآيات التي هي أفعاله وهذه مرقاة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Abraham, “that” means direct disclosure of the dominion and signs of lordship, turning sincerely from all besides God, freeing himself from ego-association, and reaching faith by direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: إراءة الملكوت وشواهد الربوبية في مرآة الكواكب وصدق التوجه إلى الحق والإعراض والتبري مما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Abraham this reality directly, without an intermediary, so he could use it as proof against his people.
rows.anchor: والإيمان الحقيقي والإيقان بالعيان آتيناها إبراهيم وأريناه بذاتنا من غير واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “come” first meant an invitation from a higher place to a lower one, then broadened to any invitation to approach.
rows.anchor: {تعالوا} أمر من تعالى والأصل فيه أن يقوله من في مكان عال لمن هو أسفل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Recite” answers the command to come and means “read”; the prohibitions are the verses that follow.
rows.anchor:
{اتل} جواب الأمر أي : أقرأ.
{ما حرم ربكم} أي : الذي حرمه ربكم أي الآيات المشتملة عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three verses contain ten comprehensive duties, unchanged across revealed books, peoples, and eras; whoever practices them enters Paradise, while whoever abandons them enters Hell.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات الثلاث إلى قوله : {لعلكم تتقون} تشتمل على عشر خصال جامعة للخير كله لم ينسخهن شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first duty is avoiding shirk, the chief prohibition, since God accepts no worship alongside it; it includes overt idol worship and inwardly recognizing anything alongside God.
rows.anchor: قدم الشرك لأنه رأس المحرمات ، ولا يقبل الله تعالى معه شيئا من الطاعات وهو ينقسم إلى جلي وخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian verse urges the troubled poet to write the declaration of unity on the page of all else.
rows.anchor:
تادم وحدت زدى حافظ شوريده حال
خامه توحيد كش برورق اين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good to parents necessarily forbids mistreatment; positive wording emphasizes that merely avoiding abuse does not fulfill their rights.
rows.anchor: {وبالوالدين إحسانا} أي : وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا ، أي : لا تسيئوا إليهما لأن المحرم هو الإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Filial duty follows the prohibition of shirk because parents are the immediate means of one’s existence; neglecting their rights is the greatest sin after shirk.
rows.anchor: لأن الوالدين سببان قريبان لوجوده كما أن الله تعالى موجده فالتقاعد عن أداء حقوقهما عقوق

rows.speaker: بعض الأولياء
rows.claim: A holy man says that serving his mother enabled him to meet al-Khiḍr in the wilderness of the Israelites.
rows.anchor: كنت في تيه بني إسرائيل ، فإذا رجل يماشيني فتعجبت منه وألهمت أنه الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse depicts Paradise as lying beneath mothers’ feet.
rows.anchor:
جنت كه سراى ما درانست
زير قد مات ما درانست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban includes burying daughters alive from poverty; imlāq means depleted provisions and expenses.
rows.anchor:
{ولا تقتلوا أولادكم} أي : لا تدفنوا بناتكم حية {من إملاق} من أجل فقر.
والإملاق
117
نفاد الزاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, rather than the parents, provides for them and their children, so fear of poverty is no excuse.
rows.anchor: {نحن نرزقكم وإياهم} لا أنتم فلا تخافوا الفقر بناء على عجزكم عن تحصيل الرزق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This third duty forbids destroying God’s creation, cutting off descendants, and failing to trust His provision, which amounts to denying His promise in 11:6.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الحكم الثالث من الأحكام العشرة ، وإنما حرم قتل الأولاد لما فيه من هدم بنيان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet counsels preserving dignity through poverty and contentment, since provision is already apportioned.
rows.anchor:
ما آبروى فقر وقناعت نمى بريم
جزء : 3 رقم الصفحة : 115
با ادشه بكوى كه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth duty forbids fornication in its forms: public brothels and secret liaisons; forbidding approach intensifies the ban.
rows.anchor: {ولا تقربوا الفواحش} أي : الزنى وجيء بصيغة الجمع قصدا إلى النهي عن أنواعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the ban covers acts and intentions that distance one from Paradise or truth, and even illicit looking.
rows.anchor: ويدخل في ذلك ما يبعده من الجنة ويدنيه من النار ، وهو ما ظهر وما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Satan tempts men and women through three bodily stations, including eyes and hearts and their sexual parts.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : "أن الشيطان من الرجل في ثلاثة منازل في عينيه وفي قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth duty protects anyone made inviolable by Islam or covenant, except where law authorizes death for apostasy, adultery after marriage, or murder.
rows.anchor: عصمها بالإسلام أو بالعهد فيخرج منها الحربي {إلا بالحق}

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Kharrāz says a dead, handsome youth smiled and told him that lovers remain alive after death, merely moving from one home to another.
rows.anchor: كنت بمكة فجزت يوما بباب بني شيبة ، فرأيت شابا حسن الوجه ميتا فنظرت في وجهه فتبسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the five duties just listed, which God emphatically enjoined so people would use reason to restrain their souls from them.
rows.anchor:
{ذالكم} إشارة إلى ما ذكر من التكاليف الخمسة.
{وصاكم به} أي : أمركم ربكم بحفظه أمرا مؤكدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach an orphan’s property in any way; an orphan is a human without a father or an animal without a mother, and the address is to guardians and trustees.
rows.anchor: {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم} أي : لا تتعرضوا له بوجه من الوجوه واليتيم من الإنسان من لا أب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the true killing is to die in pursuit of God; one killed in His path remains alive with Him.
rows.anchor: والإشارة : أن القتل الحق هو القتل في طلب الحق والمقتول في سبيل الله هو حي عند ربه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sole exception is the best way of handling the orphan’s estate, such as preserving and investing it.
rows.anchor: {إلا بالتى هى أحسن} إلا بالخصلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بماله كحفظه وتثميره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The endpoint applies to the implied duty to safeguard the estate: keep it until the orphan reaches maturity and sound judgment, then deliver it.
rows.anchor: {حتى يبلغ أشده} غاية لما يفهم من الاستثناء لا للنهي كأنه قيل احفظوه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa sets the age of maturity at twenty-five, unless the person is mentally deficient.
rows.anchor: وجعل أبو حنيفة غاية الأشد خمسا وعشرين سنة فإذا بلغها دفع إليه ماله

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari glosses ashudd as strength, spanning ages eighteen to thirty; it is an unusual singular pattern, while Sibawayh calls its singular shiddah.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري : {حتى يبلغ أشده} أي : قوته وهو ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sixth duty protects an orphan’s property because of the orphan’s vulnerability and God’s command to care for it.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الحكم السادس ، وإنما وصى الله تعالى بحفظ مال اليتيم لأنه عاجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says even the mighty throne trembles when an orphan’s heart weeps.
rows.anchor:
ألا تانكريدكه عرش عظيم
بلرزد همي ون بكريديتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill measures for measured goods and scales for weighed goods justly; qist describes the state of fair fulfillment.
rows.anchor: {وأوفوا الكيل} في المكيلات أي أتموه ولا تنقصوا منه شيئا {والميزان} في الموزونات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent repetition of justice clarifies both sides: the seller must give the full due, and the buyer must accept it without demanding extra.
rows.anchor: أمر المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه من غير نقصان وأمر صاحب الحق بأخذه من غير طلب زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because justice in measurement is difficult, people must do their best; small unintended discrepancies from diligent weighing are forgiven, while deliberate shortchanging is not.
rows.anchor: وذكره عقيب الأمر للإيذان بأن مراعاة العدل عسير فعليكم بما في وسعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One dying trader could not utter the testimony of faith because, he said, the tongue of the scales lay on his tongue, despite his claim to give full weight.
rows.anchor: يعامل الناس بالميزان ، قل : لا إله إلا الله فقال : ما أقدر أقولها ، لسان الميزان على لساني

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar visited a dying neighbor who said two mountains of fire stood before him; his family said he used separate measures for buying and selling, and breaking them did not ease his agony.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار أنه دخل على جار له احتضر فقال يا مالك جبلان من النار بين يدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the seventh duty. Inwardly, fulfill the measure of one’s lifetime and the scale of divine rights, and pursue spiritual effort and moderation according to capacity.
rows.anchor:
وهذا هو الحكم السابع.
والإشارة أوفوا بكيل العمر ، وميزان الشرع حقوق الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse says each person proceeds according to the measure of their own wings and strength.
rows.anchor: لا نكلف نفسا في إيفاء الحقوق واستيفاء الحظوظ إلا بحسب استعدادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In judgment, testimony, and speech, be just even toward relatives; truth and God’s pleasure must override kinship.
rows.anchor:
{وإذا قلتم} قولا في حكومة أو شهادة أو نحوهما.
{فاعدلوا} فيه {ولو كان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This eighth duty’s inward truth is to speak of and through God; only people of realization can do so without self-interest and claims.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة العدل في الكلام أن يذكر الله ، ولا يذكر معه غيره وأن يتكلموفي الله وبالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse invokes the hoopoe as a model for learning truthful communication and its message.
rows.anchor:
بأنك هدهدكر بياموزد فتى
راز هدهكوو يغام سبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill every covenant commanded by God, including justice and religious duties, vows to God, or agreements between people, which God requires be kept.
rows.anchor: {وبعهد الله أوفوا} أي : ما عهد إليكم أي عهد كان من ملازمة العدل وتأدية أحكام الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the ninth duty; inwardly, covenant means worshipping and loving only one’s Lord and seeing none besides Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الحكم التاسع ، وحقيقة العهد أن لا يعبد إلا مولاه ولا يحب إلا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses describe love for the Friend as one covenant extending from primordial morning to the end of time.
rows.anchor:
ازدم صبح ازل تا آخر شام ابد
دوستى ومهر بريك عهد ويك ميثاق بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder refers to the four duties just detailed and commands people to remember and act on them.
rows.anchor:
{ذالكم} إشارة إلى ما فصل من التكاليف الأربعة.
{وصاكم به} أمركم به أمرا مؤكدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal phrase means: because of what this surah has stated about divine unity, prophethood, and religious law.
rows.anchor: {وأن} بتقدير اللام علة للفعل المؤخر أي ولأن {هاذآ} أي : ما ذكر في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s “path” is his way and law, called a path because it leads to Paradise; its attribution is by following it, not by originating it.
rows.anchor: {صراطي} أي : مسلكي وشريعتي ، وسمي الشرع طريقا لأنه يؤدي إلى الثواب في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is firmly right; the other paths include Judaism, Christianity, and other religions.
rows.anchor:
{مستقيما} حال مؤكدة ، أي مستويا قويما.
{فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل} أي : الطريق المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar after the prohibition suppresses one of two successive tāʾs, and the causative bāʾ means the divergent paths separate you.
rows.anchor: {فتفرق بكم} منصوب بإضمار أن بعد الفاء في جواب النهي ، أصله فتتفرق حذفت منه إحدى التاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s approved religion is Islam, so the Prophet’s straight path is identical with God’s path.
rows.anchor: {عن سبيله} أي : عن دين الله الذي ارتضى وبه أوصى وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the tenth duty: follow God’s path and leave every other path to avoid disbelief and error.
rows.anchor:
جزدري مصطفا
{ذالكم} أي : اتباع سبيله وترك اتباع سائر السبل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet drew one line as God’s path and other lines on each side, saying a devil calls people along each side path.
rows.anchor: ولما تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية خط خطا فقال : "هذا سبيل الله"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law is a path finer than hair and sharper than a sword; people repeatedly ask for guidance to it, and deviation here means slipping from the afterlife bridge.
rows.anchor: واعلم : أن الشرع ههنا هو الصراط المستقيم وهو أحد من السيف وأدق من الشعر

rows.speaker: عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says many slip from the bridge, especially women; the author adds that most men of his time follow desires and customs like women.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "الزالون عن الصراط كثير وأكثر من يزل عنه النساء"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion has again become strange, and only a rare person offers true companionship or deserves it.
rows.anchor: والدين بدأ غريبا وعاد غريبا فلا يوجد من يستأنس به ويستأهل له إلا نادرا

rows.speaker: محققان
rows.claim: The Persian Tafsir says realized people know that all paths begin from God and end in one; Qunawi describes God’s encompassing reality or knowledge as the traveler’s beginning and end.
rows.anchor: محققان بر آنندكه صراط متعين نكردد الاميان بدايتي ونهايتي وعارف داندكه بدايت همه ازكيست

rows.speaker: صدر الدين قونوي
rows.claim: Qunawi’s teaching is that God encompasses all things, whether by existence or knowledge, making all paths turn toward Him.
rows.anchor: حق بهمه اشيا ثابت است والله بكل شيء محيط وآن احاطه وجودى است يا علمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian poem concludes that every step and every road leads through the Beloved’s street.
rows.anchor:
هرجا قدمى زديم در كوى توبود
هركوشه كه برفتيم سوى توبود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to expel the Copts and secure the land for himself and the Israelites; he issues a general threat before specifying its punishment.
rows.anchor:
{لتخرجوا منهآ أهلها} يعني : القبط وتخلص لكم ولبني إسرائيل.
{فسوف تعلمون} عاقبة ما فعلتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He threatens to cut off each person’s right hand and left foot, then crucify all of them on date-palm trunks beside the Nile to disgrace and deter others.
rows.anchor: {لاقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف} أي : من كل شق طرفا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said Pharaoh first instituted crucifixion, after which God prescribed it for highway robbers because their crime is so grave.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو أول من سن ذلك فشرعه الله تعالى لقطاع الطريق

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: The converts say they will return to their Lord through death regardless of Pharaoh’s threat, or to His mercy and reward if he carries it out; they welcome meeting God.
rows.anchor: إلى ربنا منقلبون} راجعون ، أي : بالموت لا محالة سواء كان ذلك من قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian Mathnawi depicts souls freed from body as dancing in divine love and receiving revelations after the bodily veil is lifted.
rows.anchor:
جانهاى بسته اندر آب وكل
ون رهند ازآب وكلها شاد دلدرهواى عشق حق رقصان شوند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question “what do you resent in us?” means Pharaoh has no fault to criticize except their belief.
rows.anchor: {وما تنقم منآ} أي : وما تنكر وما تعيب منا.

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: The magicians say their sole offense is believing in God’s signs when they arrived, the best deed and root of virtue, which they will not abandon to please Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: {إلا أن ءامنا بآيات ربنا لما جآءتنا} وهو خير الأعمال وأصل المناقب

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: They pray for patience that will overwhelm them like poured water as they face Pharaoh’s threat; the image is a concealed simile elaborated through metaphor.
rows.anchor: {ربنآ أفرغ علينا صبرا} أي : أفض علينا من الصبر على وعيد فرعون ما يغمرنا

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: They ask to die steadfast in the Islam God granted them, without being seduced by threats.
rows.anchor: {وتوفنا مسلمين} ثابتين على ما رزقتنا من الإسلام غير مفتونين من الوعيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Pharaoh could not overpower them because God had promised Moses and Aaron victory over their followers.
rows.anchor: قيل لم يقدر عليهم لقوله تعالى : {أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Pharaoh seized the magicians, cut them apart, and crucified them on the Nile bank.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : فأخذ فرعون السحرة فقطعهم ثم صلبهم على شاطىء نيل مصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi says the magicians knew the truth of God and surrendered their hands to the resulting punishment.
rows.anchor:
ساحران ون حق او بشناختند
دست وا در جرمها در باختند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, Pharaoh is the ego that objects to the spirit’s faith, accusing the soul’s faculties of believing before permission and conspiring with the spirit.
rows.anchor: وفي القصة : إشارة إلى أن فرعون النفس أيضا منكر على إيمان سحرة صفاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the city is the body and its inhabitants are bodily pleasures; when the soul’s qualities side with the spirit, worldly pleasures leave the body.
rows.anchor: {فى المدينة} مدينة القالب والبدن {لتخرجوا منهآ أهلها} وهو اللذات والشهوات البدنية الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ego threatens to defeat the virtues and recover bodily pleasures; it cuts their limbs from good works with the knife of false suggestion and crucifies them on worldly attachments.
rows.anchor: {لاقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف} بسكين التسويل عن الأعمال الصالحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul’s qualities answer that they return to God rather than the world, seeking patience through severing worldly attachments and death in servitude.
rows.anchor:
في جذوع تعلقات الدنيا وزخارفها.
{قالوا إنآ إلى ربنا منقلبون} لا إلى الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing Moses’ staff and white-hand miracles, Pharaoh feared him and left him unharmed; his nobles then challenged him for letting Moses and his people go.
rows.anchor: روي أن فرعون بعد ما رأى من موسى عليه السلام ما رأى من معجزة العصا واليد البيضاء خافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author states that seeking refuge is required whenever one begins Qur’an recitation, whether at a surah opening or within it.
rows.anchor: الاستعاذة واجبة على كل من شرع في قراءة القرآن سواء بدأ من أوائل السور أو من أجزائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala is required before al-Fatiha and every surah except al-Tawba, by consensus.
rows.anchor: البسملة لا بد منها في أول الفاتحة مطلقا وفي أول كل سورة ابتدأت بها سوى براءة

rows.speaker: الجعبري
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿbari’s Sharh al-Shatibiyya allows a reciter to say or omit the basmala between portions of a surah, except within al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: مخير في التسمية وعدمها فيما بين أجزاء السور سوى أجزاء براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A disavowal from God and His Messenger to those you covenanted with” means a repudiation sent from them to the treaty-breaking polytheists.
rows.anchor:
{برآءة من الله ورسوله} أي : هذه براءة مبتدأه من جهة الله ورسوله واصلة.
{إلى الذين عاهدتم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min marks the source and ilā the endpoint of an implicit “reaching”; min is not governed by the verb “disavow.”
rows.anchor: فمن لابتداء الغاية وإلى لانتهاء الغاية متعلقان بمحذوف كما تقول هذا كتاب من فلان إلى فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s disavowal means protection is severed and the pact annulled; the object is omitted as in 9:3 to avoid repeating min.
rows.anchor: والبراءة من الله : انقطاع العصمة ونقض العهد ولم يذكر ما تعلق به البراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treaties were permitted and made by Muslims with the Prophet’s approval, so they are attributed to Muslims; obligatory repudiation is God’s command and not subject to their judgment.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت المعاهدة غير واجبة بل مباحة مأذونة وكان الاتفاق للعهد من المسلمين مع رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God and His Messenger repudiated the pact made with the polytheists, who had sworn treaties; Arab groups broke them except Banu Damra and Banu Kinana, so the breakers were given four months’ notice.
rows.anchor: فنكثوا إلا بني ضمرة وبني كنانة فأمر المسلمون بنبذ العهد إلى الناكثين وأمهلوا أربعة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject “any one” is raised by a verb explained by the following clause, since in governs a verb rather than a nominal subject.
rows.anchor: {وإن أحد} رفع بفعل يفسره ما بعده لا بالابتداء لأن إن من عوامل الفعل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheist here is one whom the Muslims had been ordered to fight.
rows.anchor: {من المشركين} الذين أمرتك بقتلهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheist seeks asylum after the sacred months have ended; the Prophet must grant protection rather than kill him hastily.
rows.anchor:
{استجارك} أي : طلب منك الأمان والجوار بعد انسلاخ الأشهر الحرم.
{فأجره} فآمنه ولا تسارع إلى قتله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is protected until he hears the Qur’an concerning obligations, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor:
{حتى يسمع} أي : إلى أن يسمع أو ليسمع.
{كلام الله} أي : القرآن فيما له وما عليه من الثواب والعقاب.

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿari cites the verse to argue that one may hear God’s eternal speech, His attribute.
rows.anchor:
استدل الأشعري بهذه الآية إلى أنه يجوز أن يسمع
388
الكلام القديم الذي هو صفة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو منصور
rows.claim: Abu Mansur rejects the claim that the eternal divine attribute itself can be heard.
rows.anchor: ومنعه الشيخ أبو منصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means hearing what signifies God’s speech, just as one hears news indicating someone’s knowledge; the attribute itself is not heard by the senses.
rows.anchor: فمعنى حتى يسمع كلام الله يسمع ما يدل عليه كما يقال سمعت علم فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the protected visitor does not convert after listening, escort him to his secure home among his people.
rows.anchor: {ثم أبلغه} بعد استماعه له إن لم يؤمن {مأمنه} أي : مسكنه الذي يأمن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason for granting asylum and safe escort is that the polytheists do not understand Islam; time to hear it removes their excuse.
rows.anchor:
{ذالك} يعني : الأمر بالإجارة وإبلاغ المأمن.
{بأنهم} أي : بسبب أنهم {قوم لا يعلمون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists hold that a combatant who embraces Islam in enemy territory without learning ritual obligations owes no make-up after entering Muslim lands; one who converts within Muslim territory must make them up.
rows.anchor: حربي أسلم في دار الحرب ولا يعلم بالشرائع من الصوم والصلاة ونحوهما ثم دخل دار الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the ego and its qualities do not know God’s kindness, turn instead to worldly desire, and are graciously given time to return to obedience.
rows.anchor: فكذا النفس وصفاتها قوم لا يعلمون الله وألطافه فلا يقبلون إليه ويعملون الدنيا وشهواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Israelite youth who worshipped twenty years and disobeyed twenty saw his gray hair, feared rejection, and heard God say that He had loved, left, and patiently awaited him, and would accept his return.
rows.anchor: أحببتنا فأحببناك وتركتنا فتركناك وعصيتنا فأمهلناك فإن رجعت إلينا قبلناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant should repent and seek forgiveness promptly; youthful repentance is weightier because desire is stronger, while old age weakens its call.
rows.anchor: وينبغي للعبد أن يسارع إلى التوبة والاستغفار فإن توبة الشاب أحسن من توبة الشيخ

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi’s Persian verses mock repentance delayed until desire and worldly authority have faded, when resisting sin is easier.
rows.anchor: قحبه يراز نا بكارى ه كندتوبه نكند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse praises the young person able to sit in solitude as a lion in God’s way, despite difficulty rising from that corner.
rows.anchor:
جوان كوشه تشين شير مردراه خداست
كه يرخود نتواندز كوشة برخاست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic poem depicts an old man’s sins as too heavy for mounts, whitening his hair while darkening his heart.
rows.anchor:
شيخ كبير له ذنوب
تعجز عن حملها المطايا
قد بيضت شعره الليالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the evening” means late day through midnight; Abu al-Layth narrows it to after the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: {وجآءوا أباهم عشآء} ظرف أي في آخر النهار فإن العشاء آخر النهار إلى نصف الليل.

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth says the brothers came after the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير أبي الليث بعد العصر

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi says they came in the evening to make their excuse seem more emphatic.
rows.anchor: قال في الكواشي : وإنما جاؤوا عشاء ليقدموا على المبالغة في الاعتذار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their crying is circumstantial and means that they pretended to cry; Persian glosses it as deliberate weeping.
rows.anchor:
يبكون حال ، أي : متباكين.
والتباكي بالفارسية (كريستن يدا كردن)

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: When al-Shaʿbi assumed a crying wife in a case was wronged, Shurayh replied that Joseph’s brothers cried while guilty; judges must follow the prescribed Sunna, not tears.
rows.anchor: قد جاء أخوة يوسف يبكون وهم ظلمة ولا ينبغي أن يقضي إلا بما أمر أن يقضي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi says the brothers’ grief was a deception masking envy and malice.
rows.anchor:
كرهي اخوان يوسف حيلتست
كه درونشان رز رشك وعلتست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asks what happened to them and their sheep, and where Joseph is; they answer that the matter is worse.
rows.anchor: قال ما لكم يا بني هل أصابكم في غنمكم شي قالوا الأمر أعظم قال فما هو وأين يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nastabiq means to compete in racing or archery, each seeking to win.
rows.anchor: إنا ذهبنا نستبق} أو الرمي يقال استبق الرجلان وتسابقا إذا عارضا في السبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means useful goods such as clothing and provisions; in 12:65 it means food containers.
rows.anchor: عند متاعنا أي : ما نتمع به من الثياب والأزواد وغيرهما فإن المتاع في اللغة كل ما انتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim the wolf ate Joseph immediately after they left him, without the interval normally needed for supervision.
rows.anchor: {فأكله الذئب} عقيب ذلك من غير مضي زمان يعتاد فيه التفقد والتعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say Jacob will not believe them even if he regards them as truthful because of his intense love for Joseph and distrust of them.
rows.anchor: وما أنت بمؤمن لنا بمصدق لنا في مقالتنا ولو كنا عندك في اعتقادك صادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth reports something as it is and falsehood reports otherwise; verbal affirmation declares a speaker truthful, while inner affirmation accepts it.
rows.anchor: والصدق هو الإخبار عن الشيء على ما هو به والكذب لا على ما هو به والتصديق باللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They came over his shirt with blood” places the prepositional phrase as an adverb or circumstantial phrase; scholars dispute placing a non-adverbial circumstantial phrase before it.
rows.anchor: قميصه محله النصب على الظرفية من قوله : بدم أي : جاؤوا فوق قميصه بدم أو على الحالية منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhib is an intensive verbal noun describing the blood as false itself, or a passive verbal noun meaning falsely claimed blood.
rows.anchor: ظرفا كذب مصدر وصف به الدم مبالغة ، كأن مجيئهم من الكذب نفسه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s reading replaces the dotted letter in kadhib with an undotted one, giving a sense of turbid or fresh blood.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رضي الله عنها بغير المعجمة أي كدب بمعنى كدر أو طري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers slaughtered a kid and smeared its blood on Joseph’s shirt but forgot to tear the shirt; Jacob wept, then remarked that this was an unusually gentle wolf.
rows.anchor: روى أنهم ذبحوا سخلة ولطخوه بدمها وزل عنهم أن يمزقوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains Jacob’s accusation as meaning their own selves had embellished and made the deed easy for them.
rows.anchor: بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أي : زينت وسهلت قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God is the one sought for help” expresses continuous reliance on Him to expose the brothers’ lie and reveal Joseph’s innocence.
rows.anchor:
والله المستعان أي : المطلوب منه العون وهو إنشاء الاستعانة المستمرة.
على ما تصفون

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says the brothers’ crime preceded their prophethood, if they were prophets; his qualification signals doubt that they were commissioned.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي هذه الجريمة كانت قبل استنبائهم إن صح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author maintains prophets are protected before and after their mission from acts that repel people; the brothers’ envy, assault, throwing Joseph in the well, and deliberate lie are their own acts.
rows.anchor: وأصاب في ذلك لأن الأنبياء محفوظون قبل نبوتهم كما أنهم معصومون بعدها من الأمور الموجبة للنفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to perfect favor for Jacob’s family does not prove all brothers were prophets; it suffices that prophethood continued among their descendants.
rows.anchor: فلا يدل على نبوة غيره من الإخوان الموجودين إذ يكفي في إتمام النعمة على آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lasting word among descendants can persist even though some descendants commit shirk, so the promise does not require every brother’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى في كلمة التوحيد كلمة باقية في عقبه ، فإنه لا ينافي وجود الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ appearance as stars does not prove prophethood; Jacob is the sun of prophetic guidance and his sons are following stars.
rows.anchor: وكذا تمثلهم في صورة الكواكب لا يدل على نبوتهم ، لأنه إذا كان يعقوب بمنزلة الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If all brothers inherited prophethood, Jacob would have loved them equally from the beginning; Joseph alone was distinguished like Seth among Adam’s sons.
rows.anchor: ولوكان كلهم أنبياء لاستدعى أن يكون محبة يعقوب لهم على السوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, senses and faculties scheme and deceive, while the faith-lit spirit sees through them and patiently accepts what God’s eternal decree manifests.
rows.anchor: وفي الآيات إشارات إلى تزوير الحواس والقوى وتلبسها وتمويهاتها وتخيلاتها الفلسفية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Taʾwilat Najmiyya reads Jacob’s appeal for God’s help as asking for patience with the events of divine decree.
rows.anchor: وبقوله : {والله المستعان على ما تصفون} يشير إلى الاستعانة بالله على الصبر الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day alternate in length, brightness, activity, and rest to serve livelihood and sleep and ripen fruit.
rows.anchor: وسخر لكم الليل والنهار يتعاقبان بالزيادة والنقصان والإضاءة والإظلام والحركة والسكون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some prefer night because it serves the Lord while day serves creation, and prophets’ ascents occurred at night; al-Naysaburi also prefers night.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم قدم الليل على النهار لأن الليل لخدمة المولى والنهار لخدمة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors day in rank: night is stillness and the secret of the divine essence, while day is motion and the secret of attributes; all ranks begin and end in stillness.
rows.anchor: الليل محل السكون ففيه سر الذات وله المرتبة العليا والنهار محل الحركة ففيه سر الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred report describes God as a hidden treasure who created creation to be known; creation is meaningful motion, while before creation lay pure stillness and essence.
rows.anchor: كنت كنزا مخفيا فأحببت أن أعرف فخلقت الخلق فالخلق يقتضى الحركة المعنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Friday is the greatest day; when the Day of ʿArafah coincides with Friday, pilgrimage is multiplied seventyfold compared with other days.
rows.anchor: وسيد الأيام يوم الجمعة وإذا وافق يوم عرفة يوم الجمعة تضاعف الحج لسبعين حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s birthday is the greatest night, since without him the Qur’an would not have descended and Laylat al-Qadr would not be celebrated.
rows.anchor: وأفضل الليالي ليلة المولد المحمدي لولاه ما نزل القرآن ولا نعتت ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives some of everything people ask for, as much as He has apportioned; min can mean “some,” while all can mean abundance, as in 17:18 and 6:44.
rows.anchor: وآتيكم من كل ما سألتموه أي : أعطاكم مصلحة لكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says God provides whatever people need, whether or not they ask for it.
rows.anchor: وبداد شمارا أزهر ه خواستيد يعني آنه محتاج إليه شمابود خواسته وناخواسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s blessings cannot be counted, even roughly, because they are numerous and limitless.
rows.anchor:
{وإن تعدوا نعمت الله} بسؤال وبغيره.
لا تحصوها لا تطيقوا حصرها وعدها ولو إجمالا لكثرتها وعدم نهايتها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular definite noun “blessing” can express comprehensiveness; counting originally used pebbles to mark each decade.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن المفرد يفيد الاستغراق بالإضافة وأصل الإحصاء أن الحساب كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet says gratitude is the key to increased blessing; one seeking the treasure must not lose that key.
rows.anchor:
شكر باشد كليد كنج مزيد
كنج خوهى منه ز دست كليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, heavens are hearts, earth is souls, rain is wisdom, and its fruits are acts of obedience that nourish spirits.
rows.anchor: الله الذي خلق السموات سموات القلوب والأرض أرض النفوس وانزل من السماء من سماء القلوب ماء ماء الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law is a ship that travels the sea of the spiritual path by God’s command, never by ego or desire; a perfected guide pilots seekers to truth.
rows.anchor: وسخر لكم الفلك فلك الشريعة لتجري في البحر في بحر الطريقة بأمره بأمر الحق لا بأمر الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seekers who launch the law-ship through impulse are wrecked by desires and heedlessness before reaching the shore of reality.
rows.anchor: وكم من سفن لأرباب الطلب لما شرعت في هذا البحر بالطبع انكسرت بنكباء الأهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, rivers are esoteric knowledge, sun is unveiling, moon is contemplation, night is human nature, and day is spiritual nature; these things prepare people for divine effusion.
rows.anchor: وسخر لكم الأنهار أنهار العلوم اللدنية وسخر لكم الشمس شمس الكشوف والقمر قمر المشاهدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being given what one asks signifies an original readiness to receive divine effusion; God then grants means to rise from the lowest state to the highest.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى أعطى الإنسان في الأزل حسن استعداد استدعى منه لقبول الفيض الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world was created to support human perfection as a tree is for its fruit; the complete realized human is the fruit of the cosmos.
rows.anchor: العالم بما فيه خلق تبعا لوجود الإنسان وسببا لكماليته كما أن الشجرة خلقت تبعا لوجود الثمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessings include created things and endless divine tenderness; a person wrongs himself by corrupting this readiness through turning from truth to falsehood.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان لظلوم لنفسه بأن يفسد هذا الاستعداد الكامل بالاعراض عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Remaining good deeds” is a noun for lasting acts of good, including prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and words of glorification and praise.
rows.anchor: {والباقيات الصالحات} الباقيات اسم لأعمال الخير لا وصف ولذا لم يذكر الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet calls people to take a shield against the Fire; the shield is saying the standard phrases of remembrance.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام خرج على قومه فقال : "خذوا جنتكم" قالوا : يا رسول الله أمن عدو حضر

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi reports that some scholars interpret the lasting good deeds as daughters, whose good upbringing can save parents from the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (بعض علما برانندكه باقيات صالحات بنات است

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises a shield from the Fire to whoever is tested with daughters and treats them well; beneficence should be understood broadly.
rows.anchor: "من هذه البنات بشيء" من بيانية مع مجرورها حال من شيء "فأحسن إليهن"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting deeds are better than perishable wealth and children: their reward returns to the person, and they fulfill hopes that worldly possessions cannot.
rows.anchor: {خير} من الفانيات الفاسدات من المال والبنين {عند ربك} أي : في الآخرة {ثوابا} عائدة تعود إلى صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes boasting in worldly adornment; escape requires inward knowledge, love, and longing plus outward service, dignity, and high aspiration.
rows.anchor: والآية تزهيد للمؤمنين في زينة الحياة الدنيا الفانية وتوبيخ للمفتخرين بها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say salvation from worldly adornment requires inward beauty through knowledge and love and outward beauty through service and noble aspiration.
rows.anchor: لا ينجو من زينة الحياة الدنيا إلا من كان باطنه مزينا بأنوار المعرفة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits the Prophet’s description of the most ascetic person as one who remembers death, abandons excess, chooses what lasts, and counts himself among the dead.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قيل : يا رسول الله من أزهد الناس؟

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A divine report says worldly increase distances a believer from God, while restriction brings the believer nearer; the Prophet recites 23:55–56 as evidence that abundance is a trial.
rows.anchor: يفرح عبدي المؤمن إذا بسطت له شيئا من الدنيا وذلك أبعد له مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verses explain that God’s apparent increase in wealth and children may be a trial rather than a sign of good.
rows.anchor: {أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم فى الخيراتا بل لا يشعرون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people in view are those previously described as misguided in effort while assuming they did well.
rows.anchor: المنعوتون بما ذكر من ضلال السعي مع الحسبان المزبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieve God’s rational and transmitted signs of oneness and deny the resurrection and afterlife.
rows.anchor: كفروا باايات} بدلائله الداعية إلى التوحيد عقلا ونقلا {ولقآااه} بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds are entirely nullified by unbelief, so they receive no reward.
rows.anchor: {فحبطت} بطلت بذلك {أعمالهم} المعهودة حبوطا كليا فلا يثابون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not weighing them means despising them and assigning them no value because their good works have been erased.
rows.anchor: حبوط الأعمال {وزنا} أي : فنزدري بهم ولا نجعل لهم مقدارا واعتبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes a tall, gluttonous drinker as weighing less than a mosquito’s wing because of his worthlessness and unbelief; the scale is not set for unbelievers whose good works are erased.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بالرجل الطويل الأكول الشروب فلا يزن جناح بعوضة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation says a person’s and deeds’ weight depends on sincerity: without it neither has value, as 25:23 likens such works to scattered dust.
rows.anchor: لأن وزن الأشخاص والأعمال في ميزان القيامة إنما يكون بحسب الصدق والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about Moses may introduce the first revelation of his story in this early surah, denying prior knowledge, or may confirm that the Prophet had already heard it.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون أول ما أخبر الله به من أمر موسى فإن السورة من أوائل ما نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When he saw a fire” marks the time of the account.
rows.anchor:
{إذ رءا نارا} ظرف
368
للحديث.

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli identifies Moses’ wife as Ṣafūriyya, daughter of Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: وقال السهيلي صفورياء بنت شعيب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked to leave Midian to visit his mother and Aaron in Egypt; on a dark, cold, snowy Friday night his wife gave birth near Ṭuwa, his fire-striker sounded but produced no flame.
rows.anchor: فاستأذن منه في الخروج من مدين لزيارة أمه وأخيه هارون في مصر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Moses’ jealousy led him to travel with his family at night and leave by day, causing him to lose the company and route.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان موسى رجلا غيورا يصحب الناس بالليل ويفارقهم بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He saw a distant fire to the left of the road, thought it belonged to shepherds, and hoped to bring back a flame.
rows.anchor: فبينما هو في ذلك إذ رأى نارا من بعيد على يسار الطريق من جانب الطور

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators say Moses saw divine light rather than fire, which was called fire because that is what he thought it was.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين : إن الذي رآه موسى لم يكن نارا بل كان نور الرب تعالى ذكر بلفظ النار

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The author endorses the view that Moses truly saw fire, so his report was truthful; prophets cannot lie.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام الصحيح أنه رأى نارا ليكون صادقا في خبره إذ الكذب لا يجوز على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some Sufis say God manifested in the form Moses desired, fire, to draw his attention; a different form might have made him turn away.
rows.anchor: لما كانت النار بغية موسى تجلى الله له في صورة مطلوبة المجازي ليقبل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem says Moses saw what he sought as fire, not recognizing God manifested in light and speech.
rows.anchor:
كنار موسى يراها عين حاجته
وهو الاله ولكن ليس يدريه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hopes to find someone to guide him because fires often have people around them; hudā can mean a guide or one possessing guidance.
rows.anchor: {أو أجد على النار هدى} هاديا يدلني على الطريق لأن النار قلما تخلو من أهل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two alternatives joined by “or” need not exclude one another; ʿalā indicates people standing around or over the fire.
rows.anchor: وكلمة أو في الموضعين لمنع الخلو دون منع الجمع ومعنى الاستعلاء في على
